modules.name: Autism Information Module
modules.description: The essentials — what ASD is, how it shows up differently in every child, and what the research says about early signs.

articles.title: What is Autism Spectrum Disorder?
articles.html:
Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental condition that shapes how a person communicates, interacts socially, and experiences the world around them. "Spectrum" is the key word — no two autistic children look or behave the same way, and support needs can range widely from one child to the next.

Rather than a checklist of deficits, think of ASD as a different way of processing and relating to the world — one shaped by each child's unique wiring, environment, and relationships. Researchers increasingly describe autism as a phenomenon best understood in context: in the home, with family, and across daily routines, not just inside a clinic room.

What this means for you as a parent: your day-to-day observations at home are genuinely valuable information, not just anecdotes. You know your child's patterns better than a single assessment ever could.
articles.htmlFil:
Ang Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) ay kondisyon na may kinalaman sa paglaki ng utak. Naaapektuhan nito kung paano nakikipag-usap ang bata, paano siya nakikihalubilo sa ibang tao, at paano niya nararamdaman ang mga bagay sa paligid. Ang mahalagang salita ay "spectrum": walang dalawang batang may autism na magkapareho, at iba-iba ang tulong na kailangan ng bawat isa.

Hindi ito listahan ng mga kulang sa bata. Isipin ito bilang ibang paraan ng pag-intindi sa mundo, na hinuhubog ng sariling ugali ng bata, ng kapaligiran niya, at ng mga taong malapit sa kanya. Mas naiintindihan ang autism kapag tinitingnan sa totoong buhay: sa bahay, kasama ang pamilya, at sa araw-araw na gawain, hindi lang sa loob ng clinic.

Ano ang ibig sabihin nito para sa iyo: mahalaga ang mga napapansin mo sa bahay araw-araw. Ikaw ang pinakakilala sa anak mo, higit pa sa kahit anong isang beses na pagsusuri.

articles.title: Every Child is Different
articles.html:
Because ASD affects each child differently, the same strategy that works beautifully for one family may need real adjusting for yours. That's normal, not a sign you're doing something wrong.

  • Some children are highly verbal; others communicate mainly through gesture, behavior, or assistive tools.
  • Sensory needs vary — a sound that soothes one child may overwhelm another.
  • Routines, interests, and comfort levels are deeply individual.

The goal of this app isn't to hand you a single formula. It's to give you a range of evidence-informed options you can adapt to your own child, your own home, and your own family's rhythm.
articles.htmlFil:
Dahil iba-iba ang epekto ng ASD sa bawat bata, ang paraang gumana sa ibang pamilya ay puwedeng kailangan pang baguhin para sa inyo. Normal iyon. Hindi ibig sabihin na may mali kang ginagawa.

  • May mga batang madaldal; ang iba naman ay nakikipag-usap gamit ang pagturo, kilos, o mga gamit gaya ng picture cards o device.
  • Iba-iba ang reaksyon sa mga tunog, ilaw at hawak. Ang tunog na nakakapagpakalma sa isang bata ay puwedeng sobra para sa iba.
  • Iba-iba rin ang routine, hilig at kung ano ang komportable sa bawat bata.

Hindi isang sagot para sa lahat ang gusto naming ibigay. Gusto naming bigyan ka ng iba't ibang paraan na puwede mong iangkop sa anak mo, sa bahay ninyo, at sa takbo ng pamilya ninyo.

articles.title: Early Signs to Notice
articles.html:
Early signs can include differences in eye contact, delayed or unusual language development, strong preferences for routine, intense focus on specific interests, and distinct responses to sound, texture, or light.

None of these signs on their own means a diagnosis — children develop at their own pace. But if a pattern feels persistent and you're noticing it across different settings (home, school, with relatives), it's worth raising with a developmental pediatrician.

This is general information, not a diagnostic tool. Only a licensed developmental pediatrician or psychologist can assess and diagnose ASD.
articles.titleFil: Mga Maagang Senyales na Dapat Mapansin
articles.htmlFil:
Kasama sa mga maagang senyales ang: iba ang pagtingin sa mata, late o kakaiba ang pagsasalita, gustong-gusto ang parehong routine, sobrang tutok sa isang bagay na hilig niya, at kakaibang reaksyon sa tunog, hawak o ilaw.

Hindi ibig sabihin na may autism ang bata kung may isa sa mga ito. May sariling bilis ang paglaki ng bawat bata. Pero kung paulit-ulit mo itong napapansin at nangyayari sa iba't ibang lugar (sa bahay, sa school, kasama ang kamag-anak), magandang magpatingin sa developmental pediatrician.

Pangkalahatang impormasyon lang ito, hindi pang-diagnose. Ang lisensyadong developmental pediatrician o psychologist lang ang puwedeng magsuri at mag-diagnose ng ASD.

articles.title: Autism at a Glance
articles.html:
Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a condition related to how the brain develops. It affects how a person sees others and socializes with them, which can make communication and getting along with others harder. It also includes limited and repeated patterns of behavior.

The word "spectrum" means there is a wide range of signs and of how strong those signs are. ASD now includes conditions that used to be thought of as separate: autism, Asperger's syndrome, childhood disintegrative disorder, and pervasive developmental disorder not otherwise specified (PDD-NOS).

When signs appear

  • ASD begins in early childhood. Many children show signs within their first year.
  • A small number seem to develop as expected at first, then between 18 and 24 months lose some skills and show signs of autism.
  • Over time, ASD can make school, friendships and, later, work harder without the right support.

Why early help matters

There is no cure for ASD, but getting support early, during the preschool years, can make a big difference in the lives of many children. If you notice signs, talk to a developmental pediatrician. You do not need to wait for a diagnosis to start learning ways to help at home.

Sources

  • WebMD. (n.d.). Autism spectrum disorders. webmd.com
  • World Health Organization. (2025, September 17). Autism. who.int
  • American Psychiatric Association. (2022). Diagnostic and statistical manual of mental disorders (5th ed., text rev.). doi.org/10.1176/appi.books.9780890425787
articles.htmlFil:
Ang autism spectrum disorder (ASD) ay kondisyon na may kinalaman sa paglaki ng utak. Naaapektuhan nito kung paano nakikipag-usap at nakikihalubilo ang bata sa ibang tao. Kasama rin dito ang ilang kilos o gawi na paulit-ulit.

Ang salitang "spectrum" ay nangangahulugang iba-iba ang senyales at iba-iba rin kung gaano kalakas ang mga ito. Kasama na sa ASD ang mga dating hiwalay na pangalan: autism, Asperger's syndrome, childhood disintegrative disorder, at PDD-NOS.

Kailan lumalabas ang mga senyales

  • Nagsisimula ang ASD sa pagkabata. Maraming bata ang may senyales na bago pa mag-isang taon.
  • May ilang batang mukhang normal ang paglaki sa simula, pero pagdating ng 18 hanggang 24 na buwan ay nawawala ang ilang natutunan nila at lumalabas ang senyales ng autism.
  • Kapag walang tamang tulong, puwedeng mahirapan ang bata sa school, sa pakikipagkaibigan, at sa trabaho paglaki.

Bakit mahalaga ang maagang tulong

Walang gamot na nakakapagpagaling sa ASD, pero malaking tulong ang maagang suporta, lalo na bago mag-school. Kapag may napansin kang senyales, magpatingin sa developmental pediatrician. Hindi mo kailangang hintayin ang diagnosis para magsimulang matuto ng paraan para matulungan ang anak mo sa bahay.

Pinagkunan

  • WebMD. (n.d.). Autism spectrum disorders. webmd.com
  • World Health Organization. (2025, September 17). Autism. who.int
  • American Psychiatric Association. (2022). Diagnostic and statistical manual of mental disorders (5th ed., text rev.). doi.org/10.1176/appi.books.9780890425787

articles.title: The Three Levels of Autism
articles.html:
Today, professionals describe autism in three levels. The level says how much support a child needs with social communication and with coping with routines and change.

Level 1: needs support

The mildest level in terms of support. Children usually talk in full sentences but may find it hard to start conversations, keep social interactions going and make friends. They may struggle to organize tasks, move between activities and cope with changes in routine, and may need some help in social situations and daily activities.

Level 2: needs substantial support

Difficulties with social communication are more noticeable. Children may have limited spoken and non-verbal communication, which makes conversations and relationships harder. They may show repetitive behaviors, find unexpected changes hard and prefer steady routines. They need substantial support with daily activities and social situations.

Level 3: needs very substantial support

Children have significant difficulty with social communication, interaction and flexibility. They may speak very little, rarely start interactions and respond minimally when others approach them. They may show intense repetitive behaviors and find changes in their surroundings or routines extremely hard. They need very substantial, consistent support with everyday activities and communication.

Please note: Levels describe how much support a child needs, not who they are. A child's level is given by a qualified professional, and your child may not fit neatly into one level. Use what helps and talk to your child's doctor, therapist or SPED teacher.

Sources

  • Autism Speaks. (n.d.). ASD levels of severity. autismspeaks.org
  • American Psychiatric Association. (2022). Diagnostic and statistical manual of mental disorders (5th ed., text rev.). doi.org/10.1176/appi.books.9780890425787
  • World Health Organization. (2025, September 17). Autism. who.int
articles.htmlFil:
Ngayon, hinahati ng mga doktor ang autism sa tatlong level. Sinasabi ng level kung gaano karaming tulong ang kailangan ng bata sa pakikipag-usap sa iba at sa pagharap sa routine at mga pagbabago.

Level 1: kailangan ng tulong

Ito ang pinakamagaan pagdating sa tulong na kailangan. Kadalasan, buo ang pangungusap ng bata, pero nahihirapan siyang magsimula ng usapan, magtagal sa pakikipag-usap, at magkaroon ng kaibigan. Puwede rin siyang mahirapan sa pag-aayos ng gagawin, paglipat sa ibang gawain, at pagbabago sa routine. Kailangan niya ng kaunting tulong sa pakikihalubilo at sa araw-araw.

Level 2: kailangan ng malaking tulong

Mas halata ang hirap sa pakikipag-usap. Puwedeng kaunti lang ang salita o kilos na gamit niya para makipag-usap, kaya mas mahirap ang usapan at pakikipagkaibigan. Puwedeng may mga kilos siyang paulit-ulit, nahihirapan sa biglaang pagbabago, at mas gusto ang parehong routine. Kailangan niya ng malaking tulong sa araw-araw.

Level 3: kailangan ng napakalaking tulong

Malaki ang hirap niya sa pakikipag-usap at sa pagbabago. Puwedeng kaunti lang o wala siyang salita, bihirang magsimula ng usapan, at kaunti ang sagot kapag kinakausap. Puwedeng malakas ang mga kilos niyang paulit-ulit at sobrang hirap para sa kanya ang pagbabago sa paligid o sa routine. Kailangan niya ng tuloy-tuloy at napakalaking tulong sa araw-araw at sa pakikipag-usap.

Paalala: Ang "level" ay tungkol sa dami ng tulong na kailangan ng bata, hindi kung sino siya. Doktor o espesyalista ang nagsasabi ng level, at puwedeng hindi eksaktong tugma ang anak mo sa isang level lang. Gamitin ang nakakatulong, at magtanong sa doktor, therapist o SPED teacher ng anak mo.

Pinagkunan

  • Autism Speaks. (n.d.). ASD levels of severity. autismspeaks.org
  • American Psychiatric Association. (2022). Diagnostic and statistical manual of mental disorders (5th ed., text rev.). doi.org/10.1176/appi.books.9780890425787
  • World Health Organization. (2025, September 17). Autism. who.int

articles.title: Older Autism Terms You May Hear
articles.html:
Before the three levels, autism was split into separate diagnoses. You may still hear these names in older reports or from relatives and doctors. Today they all fall under autism spectrum disorder.

Autistic disorder (classic autism)

Significant challenges in social interaction, communication and behavior, usually noticed in early childhood. Severity varies widely: some people need a lot of support, others are more independent. Common signs:

  • Difficulty understanding social cues
  • Limited spoken communication
  • Repetitive behaviors or interests
  • Sensory sensitivities

Asperger syndrome

Considered a milder form. People often have average or above-average intelligence and strong verbal skills, without major delays in language development, but still find social interaction hard and have restricted interests:

  • Difficulty understanding social norms
  • Intense focus on specific topics or hobbies
  • Challenges in forming friendships
  • Sensory sensitivities

Pervasive developmental disorder, not otherwise specified (PDD-NOS)

Used when a person showed some, but not all, signs of autism and did not meet the full criteria for another type. Signs could include social difficulties, communication challenges and repetitive behaviors, with varying support needs.

Childhood disintegrative disorder (CDD)

A rare condition in children who developed typically for at least two years, then lost skills they had already learned in several areas, such as language, social skills and movement. It usually starts between ages 2 and 4. The cause is not well understood; it is grouped with autism because the signs overlap.

Sources

  • Little Rays ABA. (2025, March 19). Understanding the types of autism and their unique characteristics. littleraysaba.com
  • American Psychiatric Association. (2022). Diagnostic and statistical manual of mental disorders (5th ed., text rev.). doi.org/10.1176/appi.books.9780890425787
  • WebMD. (n.d.). Autism spectrum disorders. webmd.com
articles.htmlFil:
Bago ang tatlong level, may iba't ibang pangalan ang autism. Puwede mo pa itong marinig sa lumang report, sa kamag-anak, o sa doktor. Ngayon, lahat ng ito ay tinatawag nang autism spectrum disorder.

Autistic disorder (classic autism)

Malaki ang hirap sa pakikihalubilo, pakikipag-usap at kilos, at kadalasang napapansin habang bata pa. Iba-iba ang bigat: may kailangan ng malaking tulong, may mas kaya na ang sarili. Karaniwang senyales:

  • Hirap intindihin ang mga senyales ng ibang tao
  • Kaunti ang salita
  • Paulit-ulit na kilos o hilig
  • Sensitibo sa tunog, ilaw o hawak

Asperger syndrome

Itinuturing na mas magaan. Kadalasan ay normal o mataas ang talino at magaling magsalita, at hindi late sa pagsasalita, pero nahihirapan pa rin sa pakikihalubilo at may iilang hilig lang:

  • Hirap intindihin ang mga "rules" sa pakikihalubilo
  • Sobrang tutok sa isang paksa o hilig
  • Hirap magkaroon ng kaibigan
  • Sensitibo sa tunog, ilaw o hawak

PDD-NOS

Ginagamit noon kapag may ilan, pero hindi lahat, na senyales ng autism ang bata. Puwedeng kasama ang hirap sa pakikihalubilo, sa pakikipag-usap, at paulit-ulit na kilos, at iba-iba ang tulong na kailangan.

Childhood disintegrative disorder (CDD)

Bihirang kondisyon. Normal ang paglaki ng bata nang hindi bababa sa dalawang taon, tapos nawawala ang mga natutunan na niya, gaya ng pagsasalita, pakikihalubilo at paggalaw. Kadalasang nagsisimula sa edad na 2 hanggang 4. Hindi pa alam kung bakit ito nangyayari; isinasama ito sa autism dahil magkapareho ang mga senyales.

Pinagkunan

  • Little Rays ABA. (2025, March 19). Understanding the types of autism and their unique characteristics. littleraysaba.com
  • American Psychiatric Association. (2022). Diagnostic and statistical manual of mental disorders (5th ed., text rev.). doi.org/10.1176/appi.books.9780890425787
  • WebMD. (n.d.). Autism spectrum disorders. webmd.com

modules.name: Communication and Sensory Support System
modules.description: Bridging verbal and non-verbal communication, and understanding sensory sensitivities day to day.

articles.title: Visual Supports That Help
articles.html:
Many autistic children process visual information more easily than spoken words alone. Pairing speech with pictures, gestures, or simple signs can make daily instructions land more clearly.

  • Visual schedules — a simple picture sequence of the day's routine reduces anxiety around "what's next."
  • First-then boards — "first brush teeth, then tablet time" gives a concrete, visible structure.
  • Gesture + word pairing — pointing while naming an object reinforces meaning for both verbal and non-verbal learners.

Consistency matters more than complexity — the same handful of visual cues, used daily, tend to work better than an elaborate system used occasionally.
articles.htmlFil:
Maraming batang may autism ang mas madaling nakakaintindi ng nakikita kaysa sa naririnig lang. Kapag sinabayan mo ng larawan, pagturo o simpleng senyas ang sinasabi mo, mas malinaw sa kanya ang utos araw-araw.

  • Visual schedule: mga larawan ng mga gagawin sa araw, sunod-sunod. Nababawasan ang kaba niya sa "ano ang susunod."
  • First–Then board: "una, magsipilyo; tapos, tablet." Malinaw at nakikita niya ang ayos.
  • Salita + pagturo: ituro ang bagay habang sinasabi ang pangalan nito. Nakakatulong ito sa batang nagsasalita man o hindi.

Mas mahalaga ang pagiging pare-pareho kaysa sa pagiging kumplikado. Ilang simpleng larawan na ginagamit araw-araw ay mas gumagana kaysa sa malaking sistema na paminsan-minsan lang ginagamit.

articles.title: Understanding Sensory Sensitivities
articles.html:
Many children with ASD experience sound, light, touch, taste, or movement more intensely — or less intensely — than typical. A tag on clothing, fluorescent lighting, or a crowded room can be genuinely distressing, not "misbehavior."

Small home adjustments can go a long way: noise-reducing headphones for loud events, soft or seamless clothing, a quiet corner to retreat to, and warning your child before a sensory-heavy transition (like leaving a noisy mall).

Watching for your child's individual sensory patterns — what calms them, what overwhelms them — is one of the most powerful tools a parent has.
articles.htmlFil:
Maraming batang may ASD ang mas malakas (o mas mahina) ang dating sa kanila ng tunog, ilaw, hawak, lasa o galaw. Ang tag sa damit, maliwanag na ilaw, o siksikang kwarto ay puwedeng talagang nakakapagpahirap sa kanya. Hindi ito "pagpapasaway."

Malaki ang naitutulong ng maliliit na pagbabago sa bahay: headphones na pantakip sa ingay kapag maingay, malambot na damit na walang tahi o tag, tahimik na sulok na mapupuntahan niya, at pagsabi sa kanya bago pumunta o umalis sa maingay na lugar (gaya ng mall).

Isa sa pinakamagandang magagawa mo ay pansinin ang sariling pattern ng anak mo: ano ang nakakapagpakalma sa kanya, at ano ang sobra para sa kanya.

articles.title: Building Two-Way Communication
articles.html:
Communication isn't only about your child understanding you — it's also about you learning to read their cues, even non-verbal ones like a shift in posture, a sound, or a change in play.

Try responding to any communication attempt — a point, a sound, a word approximation — as a real message. This builds your child's confidence that communicating (in any form) gets a response, which encourages more of it over time.
articles.htmlFil:
Hindi lang tungkol sa pag-intindi sa iyo ng anak mo ang komunikasyon. Tungkol din ito sa pag-intindi mo sa mga senyales niya, kahit hindi salita, gaya ng pagbabago sa tayo o upo niya, isang tunog, o pagbabago sa paglalaro.

Ituring na totoong mensahe ang bawat pagsubok niyang makipag-usap: pagturo, tunog, o salitang hindi pa buo. Dahil dito, natututo siya na may sumasagot kapag nakikipag-usap siya (sa kahit anong paraan), kaya mas madalas niya itong gagawin.

articles.title: Communication and Sensory Support by Level
articles.html:
Children with ASD may find it hard to express their needs, understand others, or handle sounds, lights, textures and other things around them. Some communicate mainly through gestures, facial expressions and pictures. Knowing how your child communicates and what their senses prefer helps you understand their needs and makes everyday moments easier.

Level 1

Children usually talk in full sentences but may struggle with the "unwritten rules" of conversation: taking turns, tone of voice, body language and idioms.

  • Explain social communication openly: what an idiom means, and what a tone of voice or facial expression shows.
  • Teach them to speak up when mild sensory triggers bother them, for example to ask for noise-canceling headphones or a short break in a loud place.

Level 2

Children may speak in simple sentences or mostly about narrow interests, and their non-verbal communication may be unusual.

  • Use visual schedules, social stories and picture tools such as the Picture Exchange Communication System (PECS) so they can show you what they want.
  • Prevent overload before it happens: dim harsh lights, set up a quiet corner at home, and follow a daily "sensory diet" if a therapist recommends one.

Level 3

Children may speak very little or not at all, and find sensory input extremely hard to cope with.

  • Model and use a speech-generating device or a core vocabulary board every day, so your child has a reliable way to show basic needs or discomfort.
  • Keep their living space calm, with low noise, soft light and little clutter.

Please note: Levels describe how much support a child needs, not who they are. A child's level is given by a qualified professional, and your child may not fit neatly into one level. Use what helps and talk to your child's doctor, therapist or SPED teacher.

articles.titleFil: Tulong sa Pakikipag-usap at Sensory, ayon sa Level
articles.htmlFil:
Puwedeng mahirapan ang batang may ASD na sabihin ang kailangan niya, intindihin ang iba, o tiisin ang tunog, ilaw, hawak at iba pang bagay sa paligid. May mga batang mas gumagamit ng pagturo, mukha o larawan para makipag-usap. Kapag alam mo kung paano nakikipag-usap ang anak mo at ano ang komportable sa kanya, mas maiintindihan mo siya at mas gagaan ang araw ninyo.

Level 1

Kadalasan, buo ang pangungusap ng bata, pero nahihirapan siya sa "hindi nakasulat na rules" ng usapan: pagpapalitan ng salita, tono ng boses, kilos ng katawan, at mga kasabihan.

  • Ipaliwanag nang diretso: ano ang ibig sabihin ng isang kasabihan, at ano ang ipinapakita ng tono o mukha ng tao.
  • Turuan siyang magsabi kapag naiinis siya sa tunog o ilaw, halimbawa humingi ng headphones o maikling pahinga sa maingay na lugar.

Level 2

Puwedeng maikling pangungusap lang ang gamit ng bata, o puro tungkol sa paborito niyang paksa, at puwedeng kakaiba ang kilos niya habang nakikipag-usap.

  • Gumamit ng visual schedule, social story at picture cards gaya ng PECS (Picture Exchange Communication System) para maipakita niya ang gusto niya.
  • Iwasan ang sobrang ingay at liwanag bago pa ito maging sobra: hinaan ang matatapang na ilaw, gumawa ng tahimik na sulok sa bahay, at sundin ang "sensory diet" kung irerekomenda ng therapist.

Level 3

Puwedeng kaunti lang o wala siyang salita, at sobrang hirap para sa kanya ang tunog, ilaw at hawak.

  • Araw-araw na gamitin at ipakita ang speech device o picture board, para may paraan siyang sabihin ang kailangan niya o ang ayaw niya.
  • Panatilihing kalmado ang bahay: mahinang ingay, malambot na ilaw, at kaunting kalat.

Paalala: Ang "level" ay tungkol sa dami ng tulong na kailangan ng bata, hindi kung sino siya. Doktor o espesyalista ang nagsasabi ng level, at puwedeng hindi eksaktong tugma ang anak mo sa isang level lang. Gamitin ang nakakatulong, at magtanong sa doktor, therapist o SPED teacher ng anak mo.

modules.name: Child-Raising Behavior and Management Guide
modules.description: Practical, day-to-day strategies for routines, transitions, and calm responses to big emotions.

articles.title: Creating Predictable Routines
articles.html:
Structured, predictable routines help many children with ASD feel safe and reduce daily friction. Predictability lowers the number of unknowns a child has to process, which frees up energy for learning and connection.

  • Keep wake-up, meals, and bedtime on a consistent rhythm where possible.
  • Give advance warning before transitions ("five more minutes, then bath time").
  • When routines must change, prepare your child ahead of time rather than surprising them.
articles.htmlFil:
Maraming batang may ASD ang mas panatag kapag may malinaw at pare-parehong routine. Mas kaunti ang biglaan, kaya mas may lakas siya para matuto at makipag-bonding.

  • Hangga't kaya, pare-pareho ang oras ng paggising, pagkain at pagtulog.
  • Magsabi muna bago lumipat ng gawain ("limang minuto pa, tapos ligo na").
  • Kapag kailangang magbago ang routine, sabihin sa kanya nang mas maaga para hindi siya mabigla.

articles.title: Responding to Meltdowns with Calm
articles.html:
A meltdown is not a tantrum aimed at getting something — it's often a nervous system in overload. The most effective first response is usually to lower stimulation, not to add more instructions or discipline in the moment.

Try: lowering your voice, reducing eye contact if that helps your child, giving space, and waiting for the wave to pass before talking things through. Afterward, a brief, calm conversation about what happened (once your child is regulated) helps more than an in-the-moment lecture.

If meltdowns involve risk of harm to your child or others, consult your child's therapist or pediatrician for an individualized safety plan.
articles.htmlFil:
Ang meltdown ay hindi tantrum para may makuha. Kadalasan, sobra na ang nararamdaman ng katawan at isip niya. Ang pinakamagandang unang gawin ay bawasan ang ingay at gulo sa paligid, hindi dagdagan ng utos o pagdidisiplina habang nangyayari ito.

Subukan: hinaan ang boses mo, huwag masyadong tumitig kung nakakatulong iyon sa kanya, bigyan siya ng espasyo, at hintaying lumipas bago pag-usapan. Pagkatapos, kapag kalmado na siya, mas nakakatulong ang maikli at kalmadong usapan kaysa sa sermon habang nagmi-meltdown pa siya.

Kung may panganib na masaktan ang anak mo o ang iba kapag nagmi-meltdown siya, kumonsulta sa therapist o pediatrician niya para sa safety plan na para sa kanya.

articles.title: Positive Reinforcement Basics
articles.html:
Noticing and rewarding the behavior you want to see — specifically and immediately — tends to be more effective than only correcting the behavior you don't want.

Be specific: "I love how you used your words to ask for a break" works better than a generic "good job." Small, consistent, genuine praise builds motivation over time far more reliably than occasional big rewards.
articles.titleFil: Mga Batayan ng Pagpupuri at Gantimpala
articles.htmlFil:
Mas gumagana ang pagpansin at pagpuri agad sa magandang ginawa ng bata kaysa sa puro pagtatama lang sa mali.

Maging tiyak: "Ang galing, sinabi mo na gusto mo ng pahinga" ay mas epektibo kaysa sa "good job" lang. Ang maliit, palagian at totoong papuri ay mas nakakapagpasigla sa kanya kaysa sa paminsan-minsang malaking regalo.

articles.title: Behavior Support by Level
articles.html:
Children with ASD may find changes in schedule, following instructions and big emotions hard. You help most by being consistent, keeping routines steady, and looking for the reason behind a behavior instead of only reacting to it. Positive approaches help children build coping skills and feel safer in their surroundings.

Level 1

Challenges usually come from rigid thinking, trouble switching activities, and worry in unstructured social situations.

  • Give advance warnings before switching activities, and use a written daily planner.
  • When they feel anxious, guide them through simple coping steps such as deep breathing or talking through a problem step by step, so they learn to handle frustration on their own.

Level 2

Children often get distressed when routines change, and may show repetitive behaviors or meltdowns when overwhelmed.

  • Use visual countdown timers and "First–Then" boards so your child knows exactly what comes next.
  • Notice what sets off distress, such as sudden loud noises or abrupt schedule changes, and remove or soften those triggers ahead of time.

Level 3

Children may be very inflexible, get severely upset by small changes, and struggle to calm intense feelings. Sometimes this leads to self-injury or aggression when needs are not met.

  • Keep a highly predictable daily routine, since even small changes can cause severe distress.
  • Work with a behavior specialist on a Functional Behavior Assessment to learn what your child is trying to say during a meltdown, then teach a safe, simple sign or button press to ask for a break.

Safety first: if your child is hurting themselves or others, keep everyone safe, then ask your child's doctor or therapist for a safety plan. In an emergency, call 911.

Please note: Levels describe how much support a child needs, not who they are. A child's level is given by a qualified professional, and your child may not fit neatly into one level. Use what helps and talk to your child's doctor, therapist or SPED teacher.

articles.titleFil: Tulong sa Ugali at Kilos, ayon sa Level
articles.htmlFil:
Puwedeng mahirapan ang batang may ASD sa pagbabago ng schedule, pagsunod sa utos, at malalaking emosyon. Pinakamalaki ang tulong mo kapag pare-pareho ka, steady ang routine, at hinahanap mo kung bakit niya ginagawa ang isang kilos, hindi lang basta sinasaway. Ang positibong paraan ay tumutulong sa bata na matutong kumalma at maging mas panatag.

Level 1

Kadalasan, galing ang hirap sa pagiging "sarado" sa pagbabago, hirap lumipat ng gawain, at kaba sa mga sitwasyong walang malinaw na ayos.

  • Magsabi muna bago lumipat ng gawain, at gumamit ng nakasulat na planner para sa araw.
  • Kapag kinakabahan siya, turuan siya ng simpleng paraan para kumalma, gaya ng malalim na paghinga o pag-isip ng solusyon nang paisa-isa, para matuto siyang harapin ang inis nang mag-isa.

Level 2

Madalas siyang mainis o umiyak kapag nagbago ang routine, at puwedeng may paulit-ulit na kilos o mag-meltdown kapag sobra na.

  • Gumamit ng visual timer at "First–Then" board para alam niya kung ano ang susunod.
  • Pansinin kung ano ang nagpapagalit o nagpapaiyak sa kanya, gaya ng biglang malakas na ingay o biglaang pagbabago ng schedule, at alisin o bawasan ito bago pa mangyari.

Level 3

Sobrang hirap para sa kanya ang pagbabago, kahit maliit lang, at hirap siyang kumalma kapag malakas ang nararamdaman. Minsan, nauuwi ito sa pananakit sa sarili o sa iba kapag hindi natutugunan ang kailangan niya.

  • Panatilihing pare-pareho ang routine araw-araw, dahil kahit maliit na pagbabago ay puwedeng sobrang makaapekto sa kanya.
  • Makipagtulungan sa behavior specialist sa isang Functional Behavior Assessment para malaman kung ano ang gusto niyang sabihin kapag nagmi-meltdown siya, at turuan siya ng ligtas at simpleng senyas o pindot ng button para humingi ng pahinga.

Kaligtasan muna: kung sinasaktan ng anak mo ang sarili niya o ang iba, siguraduhing ligtas ang lahat, tapos humingi ng safety plan sa doktor o therapist niya. Kung emergency, tumawag sa 911.

Paalala: Ang "level" ay tungkol sa dami ng tulong na kailangan ng bata, hindi kung sino siya. Doktor o espesyalista ang nagsasabi ng level, at puwedeng hindi eksaktong tugma ang anak mo sa isang level lang. Gamitin ang nakakatulong, at magtanong sa doktor, therapist o SPED teacher ng anak mo.

modules.name: Learning and School Support Section
modules.description: Home-school collaboration, understanding IEPs, and reducing homework stress.

articles.title: Working With Your Child's School
articles.html:
Strong home-school collaboration helps strategies stay consistent across both settings — which matters a lot for children who thrive on predictability.

  • Share what works at home (calming strategies, communication tools) with teachers directly.
  • Ask for regular short check-ins rather than waiting for a crisis to communicate.
  • Keep a simple shared notebook or messaging thread between home and the classroom.
articles.titleFil: Pakikipagtulungan sa School ng Anak Mo
articles.htmlFil:
Kapag nagtutulungan ang bahay at school, pare-pareho ang paraan sa dalawang lugar. Malaking bagay ito sa batang mas panatag kapag alam niya ang mangyayari.

  • Sabihin agad sa teacher ang gumagana sa bahay (paraan ng pagpapakalma, gamit sa pakikipag-usap).
  • Humingi ng maikli at regular na kumustahan, huwag nang hintayin na may problema bago mag-usap.
  • Gumamit ng simpleng notebook o group chat sa pagitan ng bahay at classroom.

articles.title: Individualized Education Plans, Explained
articles.html:
An Individualized Education Plan (or a SPED learning plan) outlines specific goals, accommodations, and support tailored to your child's learning profile. It's a living document — one that should be revisited and adjusted as your child grows.

You are a core member of this planning team, not just a signatory. Bring your observations from home; they're often the most detailed data anyone has on your child.
articles.htmlFil:
Ang Individualized Education Plan (o SPED learning plan) ay nagsasabi ng mga layunin, adjustment at tulong na para mismo sa paraan ng pagkatuto ng anak mo. Hindi ito isang beses lang. Dapat itong balikan at baguhin habang lumalaki ang anak mo.

Kasama ka sa pagbuo ng plano, hindi lang taga-pirma. Dalhin ang mga napapansin mo sa bahay. Kadalasan, ikaw ang may pinakadetalyadong alam tungkol sa anak mo.

articles.title: Homework Strategies That Reduce Stress
articles.html:
Breaking homework into short, clearly bounded chunks — with visible start and end points — tends to work better than one long unstructured session.

A consistent homework spot, a visual timer, and a small predictable break routine in between tasks can turn homework from a daily battle into a manageable, structured part of the day.
articles.titleFil: Mga Paraan para Hindi Maging Stressful ang Homework
articles.htmlFil:
Mas gumagana kapag hinati ang homework sa maiikling bahagi na malinaw kung kailan magsisimula at matatapos, kaysa sa isang mahabang upuan na walang ayos.

Pare-parehong puwesto sa pag-aaral, timer na nakikita niya, at maikling pahinga sa pagitan ng mga gawain: dahil dito, nagiging maayos na bahagi ng araw ang homework sa halip na araw-araw na away.

articles.title: School Support by Level
articles.html:
Children with ASD learn in different ways and need different kinds of help. Some find classroom instructions, school tasks, classmates or the school setting hard. When parents, caregivers and teachers work together, the child's needs are better understood. Individual learning strategies, classroom adjustments and an Individualized Education Program (IEP) match support to the child, and keep home and school using the same approach.

Level 1

Focus on building independence, with help ready when a task becomes too hard.

  • Social communication practice: conversation, seeing others' point of view, friendship skills, and reading social situations.
  • Visual schedules, written instructions, checklists, and advance notice of changes.
  • School adjustments that support organization, joining in class, and flexible transitions.

Level 2

Focus on functional communication, safety, taking part, and independence in daily routines.

  • Speech and language therapy for everyday communication, and augmentative and alternative communication (AAC) when speech is not enough.
  • Structured teaching: step-by-step instruction, with praise or rewards for useful skills.
  • Visual routines and demonstrations together with spoken directions.
  • Occupational therapy for daily-living skills.
  • Home, school and therapy using the same communication and behavior strategies.

Level 3

Focus on communication, safety, comfort, taking part, and practical independence.

  • Intensive functional communication support, with a personal system that may use speech, gestures, pictures or an electronic device.
  • Highly predictable routines with visual schedules and concrete demonstrations.
  • Occupational therapy for self-care, sensory responses and daily skills; physical therapy if movement difficulties get in the way.
  • Support for other concerns when present, such as sleep problems, seizures, anxiety, depression or self-injury.

Please note: Levels describe how much support a child needs, not who they are. A child's level is given by a qualified professional, and your child may not fit neatly into one level. Use what helps and talk to your child's doctor, therapist or SPED teacher.

articles.titleFil: Tulong sa School, ayon sa Level
articles.htmlFil:
Iba-iba ang paraan ng pag-aaral ng mga batang may ASD at iba-iba ang tulong na kailangan nila. May nahihirapan sa utos ng teacher, sa mga gawain sa school, sa mga kaklase, o sa mismong school. Kapag nagtutulungan ang magulang at teacher, mas naiintindihan ang kailangan ng bata. Ang tamang paraan ng pagtuturo, mga adjustment sa classroom, at IEP (Individualized Education Program) ay tumutulong para tugma ang tulong sa kailangan ng bata, at pareho ang paraan sa bahay at sa school.

Level 1

Turuan siyang gawin ang mga bagay nang mag-isa, pero handang tumulong kapag sobrang hirap na.

  • Pagsasanay sa pakikipag-usap: usapan, pag-intindi sa nararamdaman ng iba, pakikipagkaibigan, at pagbasa ng sitwasyon.
  • Visual schedule, nakasulat na utos, checklist, at pagsabi muna bago may pagbabago.
  • Mga adjustment sa school na tumutulong sa pag-aayos ng gawain, pagsali sa klase, at paglipat ng gawain.

Level 2

Ituon sa pakikipag-usap na magagamit niya araw-araw, kaligtasan, pagsali, at paggawa ng sariling gawain.

  • Speech therapy para sa araw-araw na pakikipag-usap, at AAC (picture board o device) kapag kulang ang salita.
  • Pagtuturo nang paisa-isang hakbang, na may papuri o reward sa mga magandang nagagawa.
  • Pagpapakita kung paano gawin, kasabay ng pagsabi ng utos.
  • Occupational therapy para sa mga gawain sa araw-araw.
  • Parehong paraan sa bahay, school at therapy.

Level 3

Ituon sa pakikipag-usap, kaligtasan, ginhawa, pagsali, at mga praktikal na gawain.

  • Masusing tulong sa pakikipag-usap, gamit ang paraang bagay sa kanya: salita, senyas, larawan o device.
  • Pare-parehong routine na may visual schedule at aktwal na pagpapakita.
  • Occupational therapy para sa pag-aalaga sa sarili at sa reaksyon niya sa tunog, ilaw at hawak; physical therapy kung nahihirapan siyang gumalaw.
  • Tulong sa ibang problema kung mayroon, gaya ng hirap sa pagtulog, seizure, anxiety, depression, o pananakit sa sarili.

Paalala: Ang "level" ay tungkol sa dami ng tulong na kailangan ng bata, hindi kung sino siya. Doktor o espesyalista ang nagsasabi ng level, at puwedeng hindi eksaktong tugma ang anak mo sa isang level lang. Gamitin ang nakakatulong, at magtanong sa doktor, therapist o SPED teacher ng anak mo.

faqs.q: Is C.R.I.B.S. a substitute for therapy or diagnosis?
faqs.a: No. C.R.I.B.S. is a guidance and information tool, not a medical or therapeutic service. It does not diagnose, treat, or replace advice from a licensed developmental pediatrician, therapist, or special education professional.

faqs.q: My child was just diagnosed. Where do I even start?
faqs.a: Start with the Autism Information Module for the basics, then the Professional Support Directory to find a developmental pediatrician or SPED specialist near you. Many parents also find the parent community a helpful place to feel less alone in the first weeks.

faqs.q: How was the content in this app put together?
faqs.a: Content is compiled from published clinical and educational literature on ASD, then reviewed by developmental pediatric specialists, SPED educators, and IT professionals before being simplified for everyday use.

faqs.q: Is C.R.I.B.S. only for use in Taguig City?
faqs.a: The Professional Support Directory currently focuses on Taguig City and nearby areas, since that's where this study was conducted. The guidance content itself is meant to be useful anywhere.

faqs.q: What if a strategy in the app doesn't work for my child?
faqs.a: That's expected — every child on the spectrum is different. Treat each guide as a starting point to adapt, not a strict rulebook. If something consistently isn't working, your child's therapist or SPED educator can help tailor it.

faqs.q: Can I talk to other parents through the app?
faqs.a: Yes — the home screen includes a community feed where you can post a message or question and see posts from other parents and, where noted, from professionals.
